searchText: 0.3 wouldn’t be enough to cause TTD to come before Bellatrix. And, that’s not under the control of one entity. Say they manage to rent 0.2 of that, they’d another 0.6 to make a dent. Not trivial. Also, as has been pointed out: It’d be seen and then another update / override can be done. I am leaning towards “it’s unlikely enough to happen that having a contingency plan in the wings is sufficient” The point is that we're all guessing here, it may be easy and may not be, nobody really knows for sure if one entity has enough ASICS to cause a dent to our grand TTD plan and we have way too much faith in our ability to communicate in a timely manner a required TTD change sure but what is the contingency plan? Well the alternative is to set a very high TTD to start and then we must communicate a second client release So either release A with ludicrous TTD followed by release B with correct TTD and hope everyone upgrades Or release A with correct TTD and release B with emergency TTD only if required and if the rate drops further after the second client release? do we think we'll get enough people to upgrade a third time in a timely manner. all of this really trusts that our ability to make people upgrade is greater than I personally feel it really is (ofc thats a personal feeling) Which is why I am leaning towards having a single release with correct ttd For ux reasons If hashrate drops were fine that doesn’t cause a liveness failure You seem to be advocating for two releases because of worry of nation state adding 100% of current hashrate just to make Ethereum stall what about putting together a front page on ethereum.org with a countdown (like bordel.wtf is serving during our mainnet) and creating a "marketing" campaign to have people be refreshing that thing constantly and among other things have a TTD number there for all to see in the first line (be it the right one, the emergency one or what have you). Then maybe asking clients to add log statements in their clients directing people to that site for both excitement purposes but also as means to have a centralized point of where everybody keeps monitoring in anticipation Sure, hype is always good. The first thing to decide is how to handle the risk of ttd hitting before Bellatrix my thinking is just not leaving our communication abilities to chance.... right now we trust something is there that has never really been tested. fair point even though we agree, i want to put this out there. Medalla had all the interest in the world (and sure it was a testnet, but it was as close to the real thing as we had at the time) and the roughtime bug took days to get everybody onboard i prefer this solution myself. less moving parts if all goes well which is the scenario we should hope for Okay. So your main drive is to make sure there's clear communication on the front page of ethereum.org with a TTD countdown and, an "update now!" message, and, if we need an emergency update, then a "emergency update required, N hours to act!" thing. Reasonable. Fingers crossed EF is reading this 😄 my original solution was adding a dynamic TTD injected into clients from an outside source (be it a URL, a TXT record on DNS or what have you) but obviously that goes against the spirit of crypto in general and Ethereum in particular Yeah let's not do that So the next best thing is a place that is well known and well communicated in *advance* With clear instructions on the first line Perhaps even in the spirit of the original idea we can have clients start log spamming if the TTD they’re running on is different than the TTD on that site. Telling operators to go seek more information on that site and discord So we don’t inject anything. But we try to get people’s attention dynamically Something like a WARN level saying “Runtime TTD diverges from Ethereum.org TTD. Seek more information on official channels” Any word on how mainnet shadow fork 9 went? https://etherscan.io/block/15137572 would have been the block passing TTD? but that was like midnight UTC not the 3pm UTC estimated on whichever day mentioned here https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/892088344438255616/996758431023239209) It was planned for July 14 ~2pm UTC But looks like it is ~3pm, UTC now: https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/892088344438255616/996758431023239209 by my measure it should have merged already, no? TTD was set to 53945568722258575228928, so looks like it was hit early. https://explorer.mainnetshadowfork9.ethdevops.io/block/15137572/transactions Not sure what happened to the estimation but it was wrong by quite a few hours. Either the estimation was wrong or the hashrate changed a decent bit in the last hours. I just woke up and looking into it now. Initial look suggests that I have a config error on my side with nimbus, its fixed now and they should come online (I made a mistake while rebasing changes for my ansible configs). There seems to be one additional issue with lighthouse and the team is preparing an image to fix it(hopefully), They had an open PR for the issue with a fix and we somehow triggered it before it was merged into unstable. Some erigon nodes didn't manage to sync in time, I'm going to move to a using a snapshot made by MysticRyuujin to speed up syncing for the next time. I'll report back if there were other issues. there seem to have been a lot config errors with the forks. Are the configs too confusing? :/ Not really, but now that things are mostly stable a lot of time is spent on rebasing and merging everything into the stable setups/infra. So a high chance for mistakes there. So we have these extremely soft, changable targets of Goerli merge on August 11th and Mainnet merge in week of Sept 19th? (I am using very careful language so as not to jinx it 🐼 ) If I had to use textures, I’d say to treat Goerli as aged cheddar (not parmesan) and mainnet as burrata September is such a psychological victory, but duly noted A great victory was scored here in that devs dared to mention a date in a public call I would advise us to let Tim out of the spot for now, considering how he was pressured to give this rough timeline <:crazycry:932693133546889216> Might not hurt to push Georli even earlier by one week to Aug 4th The devs should have the time they asked for. Nethermind wanted 4, give them 4 Going to need to give a bit more than a months notice for people to upgrade nodes 😅 unlike@other forks this requires spinning up and connecting to a second node. The need for an EL node has been well known for a long time now and has been recommended since the beacon chain launch. And you can easily get an EL up in a month. I mean we have to be realistic here…dapps exchanges etc move slowly. I think kraken didn’t start testing until a month ago and I suspect most exchanges are behind them given that they are supposed to be the best There are multiple job posting for mev and eth devs on exchanges so they haven’t filled those positions yet I am being realistic. They should have already had a node ready. They've had ample notice. If they aren't ready yet giving them more time won't help. And if they really do have an issue they can raise that concern. Also, anyone can test the entire setup *today* on Ropsten, Kiln or Sepolia Obviously not the same as running through the merge, but most of the complexity of “setting up two nodes” can be tested now https://launchpad.ethereum.org/en/merge-readiness/
